scope: Post-build independent implementation audit of the released R26.15 conditions_rule edges. This is not a blind preregistration: the candidate already existed when this contract was written, so the report may establish internal semantic consistency but must not be described as external annotation agreement.

claim_boundary.certified: The changed public incident fact is an explicit input to the targeted applicable public rule, and at least one decision-record output governed by that rule changes under the frozen counterfactual.
claim_boundary.not_certified: A single rule is a uniquely necessary cause in isolation, because several applicable cricket laws can jointly govern the same output and the solver is not a modular structural causal model.

selection: For every question, independently reconstruct the sole incident-fact span for counterfactual.changed_field and each applicable rule span. The exact expected edge set contains each changed-fact-to-applicable-rule pair for which the input registry contains the changed field and the rule-output responsibility set intersects the factual-versus-counterfactual decision-record delta.

amendment_from_audit_1.trigger: A post-implementation review found that audit 1 trusted the private rule_key-to-span registration without independently checking that the target public span actually contained the frozen public rule clause.
amendment_from_audit_1.scope: Add an exact public semantic anchor check for every certified target rule span. Do not change dependencies, output responsibilities, candidate data, gold edges, thresholds or prior results.
amendment_from_audit_1.claim: This closes a certificate implementation gap; it is not a new difficulty mechanism and does not retroactively make the audit an independent human annotation.

canonical_public_rule_clauses.APPEAL: Laws 31.1 and 31.3: an umpire may not give a batter out without a fielding-side appeal made within the applicable window.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.BAT_CREDIT: Law 21.15 and the scoring laws: runs from a ball struck by the bat are credited to the striker, apart from separately recorded penalty awards.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.BOUNDARY_NORMAL: Laws 19.6-19.7: use the agreed boundary allowance; absent a different agreement, a grounded boundary is four and a qualifying bat-struck ball first grounded beyond is six.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.BOWLED_TEST: Law 32.1: Bowled requires a non-No-ball delivered ball to break the striker's wicket, including after first touching that striker's bat or person.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.BOWLER_DEBIT: The bowling analysis debits batter runs and No-ball or Wide extras to the bowler, but not Byes, Leg byes or five-run penalties.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.CAUGHT_CONTROL: Laws 33.1-33.3: Caught requires bat contact, no prior grounding, and a fair catch completed with control of both ball and movement; boundary grounding before completion prevents it.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.DEAD_SEQUENCE: Laws 20.1 and 20.6: after the ball becomes dead, a later broken wicket or later boundary contact cannot create a dismissal or boundary score for that delivery.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.DECEPTION: Law 41.5: wilful deception after the striker receives the ball makes it dead, prevents dismissal, makes the ball not count, awards five Penalty runs and retains completed plus current running.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.EARLY_DEAD: Law 20.7.1.1: when the delivered ball becomes dead before the striker had an opportunity to play it, it does not count in the over; the supported reball event records no delivery score.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.LBW_TEST: Law 36.1: LBW requires a non-No-ball delivery, a qualifying pitching and impact path, and a ball that would have hit the wicket.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.LEGAL_COUNT: Laws 17.3 and 20.7: an ordinary legal delivery counts as one valid ball unless a stated exception directs otherwise.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.NB_COUNT: Law 21.16: a No ball does not count as one of the over.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.NB_DISMISSAL_GATE: Law 21.17: after No ball, dismissal is unavailable except under Hit the ball twice, Obstructing the field or Run out.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.NB_KEEPER_RUNOUT_EXCEPTION: Law 38.2.2.2: after No ball, a striker out of ground but not attempting a run is not Run out when the wicket-keeper alone puts down the wicket.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.NB_PRECEDENCE: Law 21.12: a No-ball call overrides a Wide call at any time.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.NB_SCORE: Laws 21.14-21.15: a No-ball call adds one No-ball extra; completed runs and boundary allowances are added and classified by contact.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.OVERTHROW: Law 19.8: for an overthrow boundary, add the boundary allowance, runs completed at the instant of the throw, and the run in progress if the batters had already crossed then.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.RUNOUT_TEST: Laws 38.1-38.2: Run out requires the ball in play, a batter out of ground and that ground's wicket fairly put down, subject to the stated exceptions.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.STUMPED_TEST: Law 39.1: Stumped requires a non-No-ball delivery, a striker out of ground and not attempting a run, and the wicket fairly put down by the wicket-keeper without another fielder's intervention.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.WIDE_CONTACT: Law 22.3.1: revoke a Wide call if the delivered ball contacts the striker's bat or person before contacting a fielder.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.WIDE_COUNT: Law 22.8: a Wide does not count as one of the over.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.WIDE_DISMISSAL_GATE: Law 22.9: after Wide, dismissal remains possible only under Hit wicket, Obstructing the field, Run out or Stumped.
canonical_public_rule_clauses.WIDE_SCORE: Laws 22.6-22.7: a Wide adds one run, and completed runs or a boundary allowance from that delivery are recorded as Wides.
